subject.title: [Feature Request]: one-line local bootstrap for daemon + dashboard auth + Telegram owner setup

question: What public product shape should own localhost + Telegram owner bootstrap without weakening the pairing/security model?
rationale: The missing behavior spans installer/onboarding, gateway auth, dashboard token delivery, Telegram credentials, and owner authorization, so automation should not choose the security or public CLI contract unilaterally.

options.title: Add narrow core bootstrap
options.body: Create additive onboard/bootstrap flags or a wrapper that uses numeric owner allowlist/preapproval and documents that unattended pairing approval is not supported.

options.title: Document current composition only
options.body: Keep setup explicit and publish a supported command sequence, accepting that the common flow remains multi-step.

options.title: Split before implementation
options.body: Track Telegram owner allowlist defaults and dashboard/daemon composition as separate maintainer-scoped issues before approving a combined surface.

recommendation.title: Add narrow core bootstrap
recommendation.body: Create additive onboard/bootstrap flags or a wrapper that uses numeric owner allowlist/preapproval and documents that unattended pairing approval is not supported.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the broadest overlapping history across setup, dashboard auth, and Telegram/setup refactors in the sampled files.
